verses.english: Linked Discourses 29.21–50
1. Dragons
Thirty Discourses On How Giving Helps to Become Womb-Born, Etc.
At Sāvatthī.

verses.pali: Ekamantaṁ nisinno kho so bhikkhu bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
verses.english: Seated to one side, that mendicant said to the Buddha:

verses.pali: “ko nu kho, bhante, hetu, ko paccayo, yena midhekacco kāyassa bhedā paraṁ maraṇā jalābujānaṁ nāgānaṁ …pe…
verses.english: “Sir, what is the cause, what is the reason why someone, when their body breaks up, after death, is reborn in the company of the womb-born dragons …
moisture-born dragons …
spontaneously-born dragons?”

verses.pali: “Idha, bhikkhu, ekacco kāyena dvayakārī hoti, vācāya dvayakārī, manasā dvayakārī.
verses.english: “Mendicant, it’s when someone does both kinds of deeds by body, speech, and mind.
And they’ve heard:
‘The spontaneously-born dragons are long-lived, beautiful, and very happy.’
They think:

verses.pali: ‘aho vatāhaṁ kāyassa bhedā paraṁ maraṇā opapātikānaṁ nāgānaṁ sahabyataṁ upapajjeyyan’ti.
verses.english: ‘If only, when my body breaks up, after death, I would be reborn in the company of the spontaneously-born dragons!’
They give food …
drink …
a lamp.

verses.pali: So kāyassa bhedā paraṁ maraṇā opapātikānaṁ nāgānaṁ sahabyataṁ upapajjati.
verses.english: When their body breaks up, after death, they’re reborn in the company of the spontaneously-born dragons.

verses.pali: Ayaṁ kho, bhikkhu, hetu, ayaṁ paccayo, yena midhekacco kāyassa bhedā paraṁ maraṇā opapātikānaṁ nāgānaṁ sahabyataṁ upapajjatī”ti.
verses.english: This is the cause, this is the reason why someone, when their body breaks up, after death, is reborn in the company of the spontaneously-born dragons.”
(Each set of ten discourses of this series should be told in full the same way.)

verses.pali: Evaṁ catūsu yonīsu cattālīsaṁ veyyākaraṇā honti.
Purimehi pana dasahi suttantehi saha honti paṇṇāsasuttantāti.)

verses.english: The Linked Discourses on dragons are complete.
